newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian brands U.S. official a "gossiper".
newsitem.headline: Colombian brands U.S. official a "gossiper".

text.p: Outspoken Interior Minister Horacio Serpa branded a top U.S. anti-narcotics official a "badly informed gossiper" on Wednesday in the latest tit-for-tat outburst over Colombia's drug policy.
Serpa, embattled President Ernesto Samper's staunchest defender, was responding to comments made by U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Robert Gelbard in a meeting on Tuesday.

"Gelbard has been badly informed of what we're doing (to fight drug trafficking). And besides being poorly informed, he makes a supreme effort to gather evidence which has no basis in fact. He listens to a lot of gossip. He's a big gossiper," Serpa told reporters after a meeting legislators in Bogota.
The war of words began last week when Gelbard, in testimony in Washington, called Samper a "truly corrupt president who has a clear history of cooperating with drug traffickers."

Serpa counterattacked on Monday by dubbing Gelbard "inept, rude and brazen." The following day, the U.S. anti-drug official was reported to have reiterated remarks about Samper in a private meeting with Colombian businessmen, according to one of those present.

The mudslinging match comes against the backdrop of the United States' imminent announcement on whether it will remove Colombia from its list of virtual pariah states that have failed to crack down hard enough on drug trafficking.

The United States blacklisted, or decertified, Colombia last March in the wake of the scandal caused by allegations that Samper funded his 1994 election campaign with cocaine cash from the powerful Cali drug cartel.
